title: Daily Brief 010 — PTD lands as 2-state directive; no horizontal direct effect; Sweden walks
summary: EU Pay Transparency Directive transposition deadline passed Sunday 2026-06-07. Only Italy and Slovakia fully transposed; Poland partial; 24 member states in arrears (Germany early-2027, Netherlands/Denmark/Czech 2027-01-01, France H2-2026, Spain still consulting, Ireland slipping). Critical legal nuance most coverage misses: under settled EU law (Marshall 1986, Faccini Dori 1994) directives have no horizontal direct effect — until a member state transposes, private-sector employees CANNOT directly sue private employers under PTD. The directly-enforceable PTD compliance perimeter for Stratum's customers this week is two states plus Poland-partial; everywhere else, obligations are coming but not directly enforceable. Compass's post-mortem post needs this nuance: lead with 'directly enforceable in Italy and Slovakia; rolling implementation window everywhere else,' not 'PTD is now in effect.' Sweden is the politically distinct case Friday underweighted — Sweden published a transposition referral 2026-01-15, then reversed on 2026-03-26 and is now seeking renegotiation at EU level. The customer-facing default doctrine ('Stratum defaults to the directive's standard, not the country's status quo') needs a contingency clause for member states that publicly reject the directive. Workday Agent Passport update: the operative product Cisco brings is named — Cisco AI Defense (runtime allow/block/route/revoke control plane). Kernel and Forge's in-flight side-by-side comparison (ship 6/12) should map against Cisco AI Defense's specific capabilities, not just OWASP/NIST/MITRE benchmark categories. Three signals, top alert L4. Watch-list refresh ships today as committed.
